name: Central Retinal Artery Occlusion

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Ophthalmologic Diagnostic Criteria for Central Retinal Artery Occlusion

criteria.description: Fundoscopic evidence of a cherry-red spot at the macula
Retinal arterial attenuation and pale retina on fundoscopy
Delayed or absent retinal arterial filling on fluorescein angiography
Presence of a relative afferent pupillary defect (RAPD)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Sudden painless monocular vision loss plus fundoscopic evidence of cherry-red spot and retinal arterial pallor
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by ophthalmologic imaging; exclusion of other causes of vision loss is essential.

searchTerms: sudden vision loss in one eye
quick painless blindness in one eye

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cherry-red spot at the macula on fundoscopy
searchTerms: red spot in center of retina
cherry-red macula seen on eye exam
pupil defect indicating optic nerve damage

common.symptomName: Visual field defect (central or altitudinal scotoma)
searchTerms: partial vision loss in central or upper/lower field
blind spots in central or altitudinal vision

common.symptomName: Amaurosis fugax (transient vision loss episodes prior to occlusion)

searchTerms: headache on same side as eye

occasional.symptomName: Nausea or vomiting associated with acute vision loss
Neovascularization of the iris (rubeosis iridis) in delayed presentations
searchTerms: new abnormal blood vessels in iris
growth of blood vessels on colored eye part

rare.symptomName: Transient ischemic attacks or stroke symptoms

laboratory: Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP) if giant cell arteritis suspected
Blood glucose and lipid profile abnormalities
Coagulation studies if hypercoagulable state suspected
imaging: Fundoscopy showing cherry-red spot and retinal pallor
Fluorescein angiography demonstrating delayed or absent retinal arterial filling
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showing inner retinal layer edema
Carotid Doppler ultrasound to assess for embolic sources
MRI/MRA brain and orbit to exclude other causes
other: Electrocardiogram and echocardiography to identify cardiac embolic sources
Temporal artery biopsy if giant cell arteritis suspected

distinguishingFeatures: Visual field defect limited to a sector of the retina
Fundoscopic cherry-red spot absent or localized
Less severe vision loss compared to CRAO
Pain on eye movement may be present
Visual loss often less sudden and less severe

redFlags: Sudden, painless, severe monocular vision loss
Presence of cherry-red spot on fundoscopy
Signs of giant cell arteritis (e.g., scalp tenderness, jaw claudication)
references: Hayreh SS. Central retinal artery occlusion. Indian J Ophthalmol. 2018;66(12):1684-1694.
